study: Savage et al. 2013, ABRACADABRA (ABRA) web-based literacy
eval_evidence: ABRA was developed by a multiuniversity team (Abrami, Savage et al.); first/second authors Savage & Abrami are the program developers and conducted/authored this RCT.
developer_evidence: 'A full day of training took place led by three of the research investigators'; members of the research team also ran the demonstrations and support.
cascade_evidence: Research investigators (developers) delivered the teacher training directly; no train-the-trainer hop.
counterfactual_evidence: Control classrooms continued business-as-usual ELA instruction (control teachers received ABRA training only after the study).
coaching_evidence: Extended in-class 'just-in-time' support: RA present for the first 4 weeks plus monthly meetings; 80 just-in-time in-class support sessions documented — recurring in-class support.
student_dose_evidence: Teachers delivered ABRA to their own regular classrooms (~20 hr/child) as part of regular literacy instruction; no separate pull-out/tutoring dose (whole-class software-supported delivery).
maturity_evidence: One-semester effectiveness trial delivered once; no multi-year rollout / maturity axis.
